source: ESP-IDF master, components/soc/esp32c3/include/soc/soc.h and components/soc/esp32c3/register/soc/reg_base.h, as read 2026-08-24
verified: 2026-08-24 every memory bound and peripheral base below is quoted from the two headers above; the C3 TRM PDF was not consulted. No irq numbers appear anywhere in this file because interrupt-matrix source numbers were not verified this session

memory.name: rom
memory.why: Mask ROM, fetch bus; the reset vector enters here, and IDF/Arduino apps link ROM-resident functions via esp32c3.rom.ld, so a ROM dump (espressif/esp-rom-elfs) must be loaded or the app's first ROM call is a wild jump

memory.name: rom_dbus
memory.why: Data-bus window onto ROM constants (SOC_DROM_MASK); ROM code reads its own tables here

memory.name: iram
memory.why: 400 KB SRAM, instruction bus; app-image IRAM segments copy here

memory.name: dram
memory.why: The same physical SRAM as iram+0x4000 seen from the data bus (0x3FC80000 aliases 0x40380000); a store through one view must be visible through the other

memory.name: irom_cache
memory.why: Flash-cache window, instruction side; .flash.text is linked here. At bring-up the loader statically serves app-image bytes at their vaddrs, standing in for the cache MMU

memory.name: drom_cache
memory.why: Flash-cache window, data side; .flash.rodata. Same static-mapping stand-in

memory.name: rtc_ram
memory.why: 8 KB RTC FAST memory, mapped identically on both buses (SOC_RTC_IRAM equals SOC_RTC_DRAM)

peripherals.name: UART0
peripherals.why: An RX read pops a FIFO - impure. TX-status read-0 happens to mean empty so prints drain, but the bytes must land in the session's serial event stream

peripherals.name: SPI1
peripherals.why: The flash controller the esp_flash driver commands directly; nvs_flash_init in Arduino's init reads the NVS partition through it

peripherals.name: SPI0
peripherals.why: Cache-fill engine; firmware rarely touches it directly - the access accounting will say if that assumption is wrong

peripherals.name: GPIO
peripherals.why: OUT/W1TS/W1TC writes emit pin events; IN carries button state inward - impure both directions. digitalWrite ends here, and the visible blink is this peripheral's output

peripherals.name: RTC_CNTL
peripherals.why: Upgraded from stub after reading rtc_clk.c/rtc_init.c/rtc_time.c: the TIME counter is load-bearing (the ocode regi2c poll's only escape is a timeout computed from it), STORE4/5 stash XTAL/APB frequencies, and SLOW_CLK_NEXT_EDGE is a genuine self-clearing bit. The RWDT/SWD watchdog block is deliberately NOT listed in the regmap so the unknown-offset default keeps it inert - a half-coded watchdog is worse than an inert one

peripherals.name: EFUSE
peripherals.why: The bootloader compares the image's min_chip_rev_full against the efuse wafer version; all-zero efuse reads rev v0.0 and modern images refuse to boot (IDF C3 default min rev v0.3 - not re-verified this session). Needs a regmap with nonzero revision reset values drafted from efuse_reg.h; PICSimLab's C3 board writes wafer-minor=3 for exactly this reason

peripherals.name: IO_MUX
peripherals.why: Pure pin-function storage at bring-up; reads-as-written serves the RMW config patterns

peripherals.name: TIMG0
peripherals.why: Forced coded by RTCCALICFG1.VALUE arithmetic and by RDY depending on two source bits - see peripherals/esp32c3/timg-contract.json. The MWDT0 half stays inert at bring-up for the RTC_CNTL reason

peripherals.name: TIMG1
peripherals.why: MWDT1 and the second calibration unit; same contract

peripherals.name: SYSTIMER
peripherals.why: FreeRTOS tick and esp_timer source: counter reads derive from cycles, but the alarm comparators raise interrupts - a side effect no kind expresses. Without it vTaskDelay never wakes: blink toggles once and stops

peripherals.name: USB_SERIAL_JTAG
peripherals.why: The XIAO ESP32-C3 has no UART bridge and Arduino defaults CDC-on-boot=1, so Serial writes land here, not UART0. A simple FIFO+status pair; status read-0 means space-available so prints drain

peripherals.name: SYSTEM
peripherals.why: Adopted by ruling 2026-08-24: esp-soc-2's regmap (strict superset of esp-soc's retired system.json - adds PERIP_CLK_EN0/PERIP_RST_EN0 gating - and pins an IDF tag). The C3 clock switch is write-and-fixed-delay with no SWS-style handshake, verified independently by both agents; every field is plain storage

peripherals.name: INTMATRIX
peripherals.why: Espressif-custom source-to-CPU-line routing - no CLINT or PLIC exists on any ESP RISC-V chip, so a stock RISC-V platform model cannot substitute. Boundary question for the design's section 3: the CPU-side INTC priority/claim registers are this chip's SCS-analogue and arguably belong in-core, with only this routing matrix outboard

peripherals.name: EXTMEM
peripherals.why: Cache/MMU control. The loader's static flash mapping stands in until firmware calls esp_partition_mmap or the flash driver suspends the cache; accounting on this stub is the tripwire that says the stand-in has run out
